newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, September 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, September 25.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

*Labour minister Tiziano Treu has signed a labour pact with representatives of trade unions and Confindustria (Italian industry association). Some 15 trillion lira will be spent in the next three years to support labour policies and to create new jobs, especially in Southern Italy (all).

*Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti insists he will oppose any proposed cuts in pensions and healthcare in the 1997 budget, while he might accept an extra "tax for Europe" (Corriere).
*Lower house speaker Luciano Violante has proposed the creation of a special parliamentary commission against corruption (la Repubblica).

* Ahead of a new government meeting with the majority party leaders, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi is expected to raise the cost of retirement benefits by an extra 0.5 pct on revenues in the 1997 budget (all).

* September inflation rates in the second group of sample cities (from 0.0 to 0.4 pct) reassure analists after disappointing results from the first group. Forecasts now see a year-on-year 3.4 pct increase (Sole 24 Ore).
* Enzo Berlanda, chairman of Italy's stock exchange watchdog authority Consob, says the body still has doubts over the validity of Olivetti's first half 1996 financial statement (Sole 24 Ore).
* Italian top merchant bank Mediobanca posted a 1995-96 net profit of 120.3 billion lire, down from 155 billion, due to a fall in the value of its investment securities portfolio (Sole, Corriere).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
